family: a script CI invokes that lacks execute permission
description: CI runs ./stats.py directly, but the file is not executable
replace:
run: python -m pytest tests -v
      - name: Summarise evaluation results
        run: ./stats.py

  docker:
notes: Expected behaviour below is predicted from the code, not yet observed in CI; check it against the saved log. A new last step runs ./stats.py. The file is tracked with mode 100644 (no file in the repository is executable), so the checkout has no execute bit and bash fails with './stats.py: Permission denied', exit code 126, before stats.py runs at all. pytest runs first and passes (13 passed), so the job fails after a green test summary; failing step 'Summarise evaluation results'. Fix: 'python stats.py'. Committing the file as executable would not fix it on its own: stats.py has no shebang, so bash runs it as a shell script ('from: command not found', then a syntax error, exit 2); that also needs a '#!/usr/bin/env python3' line. The repository has no executable script, so the case invokes an existing non-executable file instead of adding one; this keeps it to one find/replace in one file. Local check (2026-11-20, python:3.11 container, git clone of the repository at ad2be2f): git ls-files -s and ls -l show 100644 / -rw-r--r--, and running the step script with bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail printed './stats.py: Permission denied' (prefixed by the script path and 'line 1:') with exit 126. The pytest part of the job was not run in this check.
